name: Ddelta and chunk-context-aware resemblance detection. Two coupled lines. (a) Ddelta: Xia, Jiang, Feng, Tian, Fu, Zhou, 'Ddelta: A deduplication-inspired fast delta compression approach', Performance Evaluation 79 (2014) 258-272 - the paper that introduced the Gear hash. (b) The resemblance-detection family that decides WHICH base chunk to delta against: super-features / N-transform (Broder shingling; Shilane et al., Data Domain WAN-optimised replication, 2012), REBL and its First-Fit rule (Kulkarni et al. 2004), Finesse (Zhang et al., FAST 2019), and CARD - 'Chunk Content is not Enough: Chunk-Context Aware Resemblance Detection for Deduplication Delta Compression', Ye, Xue, Tian, Xu, Xiao, Li, arXiv:2106.01273, 2021. Adjacent: Odess, DARE (duplicate-adjacency-based resemblance detection), Xdelta and Zdelta as the classic delta encoders.
kind: Research results plus algorithm families. Ddelta is a published algorithm with a prototype; the resemblance-detection methods are research results, of which super-features/N-transform is the only one with confirmed large-scale production deployment (Data Domain). CARD is a research prototype in Python with a trained neural network. None is a standard, a browser feature, or a service.
maturity: Split sharply. Super-feature resemblance detection plus delta encoding is PRODUCTION - it is the post-deduplication data reduction stage in commercial backup appliances and WAN replication. Ddelta is a published prototype whose most important component, the Gear hash, went on to production ubiquity via FastCDC and Hugging Face Xet, while Ddelta's own delta encoder did not. Finesse is a peer-reviewed FAST'19 result with an open implementation. CARD (2021) is a research prototype only: a Python implementation, an unreleased trained BP-neural-network model, evaluated on three datasets, with no follow-on deployment found. Treat CARD as an idea, not a component.
license: Ddelta and Finesse are published papers; the algorithms are unencumbered. Xdelta is GPL/Apache-family, Zdelta is a research release, Spooky hash is public domain, Gear hash implementations are MIT/Apache. CARD's prototype has no license or artifact found in this research - the paper points to no repository. Nothing here blocks use of the ALGORITHMS in this project. [uncertain] on CARD artifact availability and license; none located.
keeps_and_discards: Delta encoding is lossless by construction: base plus delta reconstructs the target byte-for-byte, so nothing is discarded from the content. What the family discards is INDEPENDENCE. After delta encoding, a chunk is no longer self-describing - reading it requires reading its base chunk, and possibly that base's base. For a page store this is the substantive trade: the trie's current property that every node is readable from its own row is given up in exchange for space. The resemblance-detection half discards something more consequential and less obviously: it discards CANDIDATES. Super-features, Finesse and CARD are all lossy filters that decide two chunks are 'similar enough' to attempt a delta; a false negative means the redundancy exists and is silently kept, while a false positive means a wasted read and a poor delta. Ddelta's own measurements show what the greedy layer recovers on top of that: Step 1, greedily scanning inward from both ends of two similar chunks with NO chunking or fingerprinting at all, finds about one third of the redundancy by itself.
structure_preserved: None whatsoever, on both halves. Delta encoding is a byte-level copy/insert instruction stream; resemblance detection is a set of hashes over byte ranges. Nesting, order beyond sequence, tabular relations and shadow boundaries are all invisible. The one structural notion present is ADJACENCY - Ddelta's Step 3 and the DARE line exploit the fact that duplicate regions cluster next to other duplicate regions, and CARD's whole thesis is that a chunk's NEIGHBOURING chunks carry signal about it. That is a linear-stream notion of context, not a tree notion, and it does not transfer directly to a trie where a node's neighbours are siblings and its parents are ancestors. Translating CARD's chunk-context idea to a DOM trie would mean 'a node's re-anchoring is informed by its siblings and parent', which is a legitimate idea but is a different algorithm from the one CARD evaluated.
interactive_elements: Not handled. Neither delta encoding nor resemblance detection has any notion of a control, a role, or an event handler. A control's serialised text is bytes like any other. Any interactivity marking must be established above this layer and, importantly, must be excluded from the delta stream if it is to remain cheaply queryable - a control whose state lives inside a delta-encoded blob cannot be read without reconstructing the blob.
interactive_state_fidelity: Zero intrinsically, and delta encoding actively worsens the ACCESS cost of whatever state is carried. States that are byte-identical between base and target cost nothing in the delta; states that flip become copy/insert instructions. The important asymmetry for this project is on read: a disabled or aria-expanded flag stored inside a delta-encoded payload requires materialising the base chain before it can be inspected, which turns a cheap attribute lookup into a multi-read reconstruction. That argues strongly for the same separation FastCDC argues for - interactive state belongs in the key or in an unencoded attribute vector, never inside the payload subject to delta compression. There is no published measurement of state fidelity here because the field never represents state at all.
layout_awareness: None at any stage. No geometry, no computed style, no bounding boxes. Fully compliant with no_layout_in_the_fold, and with the same mirror-image blindness as CDC: a change altering only rendering produces an identical byte stream and therefore an empty delta, so it is reported as no change.
javascript_required: No. Both halves are pure post-capture computation over byte streams, running outside the browser. No page code fires, no DOM API is touched, no telemetry can be triggered by them. CARD adds a neural-network inference step, which is still pure local computation but introduces a model dependency (see no_mocks in the ledger).
evaluation_method: Ddelta: a prototype in a post-deduplication data reduction pipeline (deduplicate -> resemblance-detect -> read base chunk -> delta encode -> GZ), measuring compression factor at each stage, delta encoding and decoding throughput, and a sensitivity sweep over average string size. Baselines are Xdelta and Zdelta, both established encoders, which makes the comparison meaningful. Notably Ddelta also runs a component ablation - Rabin+SHA1 vs Gear+SHA1 vs Rabin+Spooky vs Gear+Spooky - which correctly attributes speedup to each substitution rather than claiming it all for the new algorithm. CARD: a Python prototype on a three-machine simulated cloud, measuring Delta Compression Ratio (total size before / total size after) and total wall-clock resemblance-detection time, against N-transform and Finesse, with FastCDC as the common chunker and Xdelta as the common encoder, swept over average chunk size 16 KB to 512 KB and feature dimension 40 to 80. The pervasive methodological weakness across the family: the metric is aggregate compression ratio, NOT per-chunk detection precision and recall, so a scheme's false-negative rate - the thing that actually matters for a delta guarantee - is never reported directly.
corpus_size_and_origins: Ddelta used six datasets, all versioned artifacts, none of them web pages: GCC (43 versions, 14.1 GB), Linux (258 versions, 104 GB), VM-A (78 images, 114 GB - a mix of 23 CentOS, 18 Fedora, 17 Ubuntu, 12 FreeBSD, 6 Debian), VM-B (117 full backups of one in-use Ubuntu 12.04 VM, 1.78 TB), RDB (211 Redis dump.rdb snapshots, 1.15 TB), Bench (200 snapshots from a personal-cloud-storage benchmark, 1.54 TB). CARD used three: a VMDK backup trace from 6 members of a university research group (Zhou et al. 2015), a SQL dump workload (Beller et al. 2017), and Linux Kernel versions (Tian et al. 2018). Sizes are not stated for CARD's datasets. THE DECISIVE GAP FOR THIS PROJECT: there is not a single web page, HTML document or DOM subtree in any of these nine datasets. Every corpus is large versioned binary or source artifacts with strong sequential locality between consecutive versions - exactly the shape that makes delta compression look good and exactly not the shape of many small independently-addressed strings. Any number quoted from this literature must carry that: it was measured on VM images and kernel trees, from 2014 and 2021, at file and multi-KB-chunk granularity.
reported_precision_recall: The family reports compression ratios and speedups, not precision and recall, and the absence is itself a finding. DDELTA: encoding speedup of 2.5x over Xdelta and 8x over Zdelta on average (configured with an average string size of 32 BYTES), decoding speedup 2x-20x, at comparable data reduction. Component ablation: Spooky-instead-of-SHA1 contributes about 1.7x, Gear-instead-of-Rabin about 1.4x, and Gear-based chunking alone is about 2.1x faster than Rabin-based chunking. Gear vs Rabin at 8 KB target across all six datasets differs in compression ratio by 0.001% to 0.329% and in real average chunk size by 0.008 to 1.144 KB - i.e. substituting the cheap hash for the expensive one costs essentially nothing in deduplication quality, which is the finding that made Gear the default everywhere. Post-deduplication compression factors (Ddelta Table 5): delta compression contributes CF 1.55 to 5.29 on top of deduplication, GZ a further 1.00 to 3.09. CARD: up to 75.03% more redundant data detected, and 5.6x to 17.8x faster resemblance detection, against N-transform and Finesse. Specific CARD points: on SQL dump at 16 KB chunks, DCR improved 45.49% over N-transform and 51.19% over Finesse, and CARD was 6x faster than Finesse and 11x faster than N-transform; on VMDK at 256 KB chunks CARD was 5.6x faster than Finesse and 17.88x than N-transform. Also from Ddelta's related-work survey, a useful production number: Shilane et al. report average delta encoding speed for similar chunks in the range 30-90 MB/s, described as a potential storage-system bottleneck. The published FALSE-NEGATIVE analysis that does exist is analytic rather than measured: CARD shows that under Finesse, a modification touching the maximum Rabin value of the first sub-chunk gives a 33.3% probability that the chunk's feature differs and the chunk is therefore missed as a similarity candidate.
independent_oracle: For the delta half, yes and it is complete: apply the delta to the base and compare to the target. This is assumption-free, shares nothing with the encoder, and is cheap. Ddelta's own design leans on it (the encoder is allowed to use a weak 64-bit Spooky hash for string matching precisely because a full content comparison verifies matches before they are emitted, so a hash collision costs time rather than correctness - the algorithm explicitly checks content on Spooky match). For the resemblance-detection half there is NO independent oracle in the literature and this is a serious gap: the ground truth of 'which chunk is the best base for this chunk' would require an all-pairs comparison that nobody runs, so every reported improvement is measured against an aggregate compression ratio that shares the whole pipeline's assumptions. Nothing equivalent to the impartial Delft/Darmstadt reimplementation that exists for CDC exists for resemblance detection: no third party has reproduced Finesse's or CARD's numbers. For CARD specifically the oracle problem is compounded - its output depends on a trained model whose weights are not published.
evidence_independence: Poor and worsening down the chain. Ddelta is author-run by the group (Xia, Jiang, Feng) that also produced FastCDC and, later, Finesse - so Ddelta, FastCDC and Finesse are substantially the same research programme evaluating itself, which means their mutual citations are not independent corroboration. CARD is author-run by a different group (University of South China / Suffolk / VCU / HUST), which makes its criticism of Finesse genuinely third-party and is the most valuable independent element in this item: an outside group demonstrating an analytic failure mode (the 33.3% miss probability) in the incumbent method. But CARD's own numbers are then author-run in turn, on a Python prototype, with an unpublished model. The one broadly independent number in the whole item is Shilane et al.'s 30-90 MB/s delta encoding range, which comes from a production vendor measuring its own shipping system - vendor-run, but at least on real deployed workloads rather than a prototype.
page_archetype_coverage: None. There are no web pages in any evaluation, so there is no article / forum / product / collection / listing / documentation / service breakdown and no basis for one. What the datasets DO stratify by is entropy and modification pattern, and that stratification carries a transferable warning: CARD reports that its own method's advantage collapses on VMDK and Linux Kernel because 'some modification patterns tend to be random which is no conductive to the chunk-context embedding', with DCR flat at 3.29 and 3.69 across every feature dimension from 40 to 80 - i.e. the context signal exists only where changes are structured, and vanishes where they are diffuse. Mapped onto page archetypes, that predicts context-aware detection would help on documentation and article pages that change in localised edits, and do nothing on listing, feed and service pages that change diffusely everywhere. That is a prediction from the authors' own admitted failure, not a measurement.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Byte-level throughout and therefore script-invariant in the same way as CDC: Gear indexes a 256-entry table by byte, Spooky and Rabin hash bytes, and delta instructions are byte offsets. No tokeniser, no word boundary, no whitespace assumption, so CJK, RTL and whitespace-free text behave identically. Two consequences. First, delta instruction boundaries can split UTF-8 codepoints, so a delta-encoded payload is not partially decodable as text. Second, and more interesting, Ddelta's average string size of 32 bytes is roughly 32 ASCII characters but only ~10 CJK characters, so the string-level matching granularity is 3x finer in CJK by character count - which should if anything help, but is untested. CARD's neural context model is the exception: it is TRAINED on a dataset, so it is dataset-tuned and by extension locale-tuned, and a model trained on English source code and SQL dumps has no established behaviour on other scripts. [uncertain] on all locale behaviour; no evaluation in the family uses non-Latin text.
leaks_outward: The algorithms disclose nothing to the page - they run after capture, out of process. The disclosure risk is in the stored artifact and it is materially WORSE than plain CDC in one specific way: a delta-compressed store makes the SIMILARITY RELATION between stored items explicit and queryable. Where a chunk index leaks that two pages share a block, a delta store leaks that page B was encoded against page A and by how many instructions, which is a much richer signal. The chunking-attack literature already established that chunk-length sequences fingerprint content; a delta instruction stream's length and structure is a strictly stronger fingerprint of the DIFFERENCE between two documents. Combined with the resemblance index - a super-feature is a hash of content features, which is a locality-sensitive sketch and therefore inherently more informative than a cryptographic hash - the resemblance index is closer to an embedding than to a digest and should be treated as sensitive derived data. If none of this leaves the local store it reduces to nothing; if a resemblance index is ever shared or exported, it discloses approximate content.
mechanism_detectability: Zero. No browser API is patched, no CDP domain enabled, no extension installed, no script injected. Everything happens after the page has been read and out of the page's process, so nothing about adopting delta compression or resemblance detection is observable by a page, and closed shadow roots are untouched. CARD's neural inference is likewise local. This is a clean pass on closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed - the technique adds no detection surface at all.
countermeasures: For the correctness risks: verify every delta by applying it and comparing to the target before committing (Ddelta's own Spooky-collision handling is the in-algorithm version of this, checking string content on hash match), and bound base-chain depth so reconstruction cost is capped rather than unbounded. For the resemblance false-negative risk: nothing in the literature; the only real countermeasure is to accept that missed similarity costs space, never correctness, which is what makes the family safe to adopt speculatively. For the leakage risks: keep the resemblance index local and treat it as content-equivalent, not as a hash. For CARD specifically: the countermeasure is not to adopt the neural model at all, since its determinism, reproducibility and no-mocks posture are all compromised by a trained artifact, and its measured benefit vanishes on diffusely-changing data anyway.
measured_fidelity_cost: Delta encoding is lossless, so there is no fidelity cost to measure - the costs are in time and access. Measured, with controls: substituting Gear for Rabin costs 0.001%-0.329% in compression ratio across six datasets (control: Rabin at the same 8 KB target) while gaining ~2.1x chunking speed; substituting Spooky for SHA-1 gains ~1.7x encoding speed with correctness preserved by explicit content verification on match. The string-size sweep is the most useful measured trade for this project: Ddelta's compression ratio DECREASES and its encoding speed INCREASES as average string size grows, and the authors settled on 32 bytes as the operating point - a very fine granularity chosen deliberately, at a throughput cost, because finer strings find more redundancy. That is a directly relevant measured data point against the assumption that content-defined segmentation must operate at kilobyte scale. For CARD, the measured cost of raising feature dimension from 40 to 80 is +13% to +41% wall time (SQL dump 1514.86 -> 1715.07 s; Linux Kernel 3073.52 -> 4344.69 s; VMDK 3681.18 -> 3824.97 s) for DCR gains of +3.62%, +0.91% and 0.00% respectively - i.e. on two of three datasets the extra dimensions bought essentially nothing.
gate_state_at_capture: Not represented and not inferable. The family has no notion of consent banners, paywalls, login walls or CAPTCHAs. The specific hazard delta compression introduces is that a gated and an ungated capture of the same URL are highly similar by construction - the stub is a prefix-ish subset of the full article - so resemblance detection will confidently pair them and delta-encode one against the other. Without gate state in the key that produces a store in which the paywalled stub and the full article are entangled as base and delta, with no record of which is which, and deleting or re-fetching one damages access to the other. Gate state must be part of the address before delta encoding is applied, not after.
determinism: Ddelta and the classical resemblance methods: fully deterministic. Same inputs, same table, same parameters, same super-feature configuration -> identical delta streams and identical similarity decisions, on every platform. Ddelta's use of a weak 64-bit Spooky hash does not compromise this because collisions are resolved by explicit content comparison, so a collision changes timing, not output. ONE ORDER-DEPENDENCE that must be named: the First-Fit rule inherited from REBL means that when resemblance detection surfaces several candidate bases, the FIRST match is selected - so the delta stream depends on insertion order into the index, and re-ingesting the same corpus in a different order produces a different (equally valid, differently sized) store. That is determinism of the reconstructed content but NOT determinism of the stored artifact, and any reproducibility claim must say which of the two it means. CARD is a separate case: deterministic given fixed trained weights, but the weights are the output of a stochastic training process with random initialisation, so CARD is only as deterministic as its model checkpoint is pinned and published - and it is not published.
determinism_across_versions: No browser dependency, so none of the AX-tree or CDP drift classes apply. Drift is parametric and, as with CDC, total when it occurs: changing the Gear table, the string-size target, the number of super-features, the features per super-feature, or Finesse's sub-chunk count changes which chunks are found similar and therefore changes every delta in the store. The super-feature configuration is a particularly load-bearing constant - Ddelta used 3 super-features of 2 features each, and that tuple must be versioned with the index. For CARD the version problem is qualitatively worse: retraining the model on new data silently changes similarity decisions with no parameter to inspect, which means a CARD-based store cannot state what version of its own similarity function produced it unless model checkpoints are versioned as first-class artifacts. That alone disqualifies it from a reproducibility-bearing path here.
reproducibility: The delta encoders are reproducible from bytes alone with no browser, no network and no model - as strong as CDC. The resemblance layer is reproducible in the classical methods (super-features, Finesse) given the parameter tuple, with the First-Fit order caveat above. CARD is NOT reproducible in any practical sense: no published artifact, no published model weights, a Python prototype, and results that depend on training data. The corpora are mixed: Ddelta's GCC and Linux datasets are reconstructible from public archives, but the VM-A/VM-B/RDB/Bench traces are private, and CARD's three datasets are cited to other papers rather than published, so no third party can rerun either evaluation exactly. Practical rule for this project: the delta/verify mechanism is reproducible and adoptable; the published NUMBERS are not independently re-obtainable and should be treated as directional.
failure_modes: Six. (1) RESEMBLANCE FALSE NEGATIVE - two chunks are similar but no feature matches, so the redundancy is silently kept. CARD's analysis puts a number on the incumbent's version of this: a modification affecting the first sub-chunk's maximum Rabin value gives Finesse a 33.3% chance of missing the pair, purely from permutation of the grouped ranks. (2) SIZE MISMATCH - the same analysis shows that two similar chunks of DIFFERENT sizes get different sub-chunk boundaries and therefore mostly different features, so similar-but-resized content is systematically missed. For a DOM store where a node grows or shrinks between visits, this is the common case, not the rare one. (3) RESEMBLANCE FALSE POSITIVE - a base is read (a random I/O, which Ddelta notes is why base reads dominate) and yields a poor delta; cost is time and space, not correctness. (4) BASE-CHAIN DEPTH - a delta encoded against a delta encoded against a delta makes read cost linear in chain length and makes any single corruption fatal for the whole chain. (5) DIFFUSE MODIFICATION - CARD's own admitted failure: where changes are randomly distributed rather than localised, context embedding contributes nothing and DCR flattens completely. (6) THROUGHPUT WALL - delta encoding of similar chunks runs at 30-90 MB/s in production measurement, one to two orders of magnitude slower than chunking, so delta encoding is the pipeline bottleneck by a wide margin.
failure_visibility: Structurally split, and the split is favourable. The delta half fails LOUDLY and verifiably: applying a delta and comparing to the target catches every encoder error, and the check is cheap enough to run on every write. The resemblance half fails SILENTLY and by design - a missed similarity is indistinguishable from an absent similarity, and no reported metric exposes it. The literature's own aggregate metric (compression ratio) hides this completely: a scheme that misses half the similar pairs still reports a respectable ratio. For this project the operational consequence is precise and cheap to act on: if resemblance detection is ever adopted, the honest instrumentation is not compression ratio but a periodic sampled all-pairs check on a small holdout to estimate the miss rate - otherwise the layer's degradation is unobservable, which is exactly the anti-pattern this project refuses. CARD adds a third and worse category: a retrained or drifted model changes similarity decisions with no error, no log line and no inspectable parameter.
scale_limits: Two separate walls, and the second one is directly relevant to the ingest-degradation problem. FIRST, the resemblance index: every chunk contributes several super-features to a lookup structure, and detection is a probe into it - the same random-access-into-a-growing-index shape as the CDC chunk index, with the same property that its cost is a memory-hierarchy step function invisible to a call profiler. Worse than the CDC index, because a chunk contributes MULTIPLE feature rows rather than one, so the structure grows several times faster per unit of content. CARD's own numbers show the growth: raising feature dimension from 40 to 80 raised Linux Kernel wall time from 3073 s to 4344 s (+41%) for zero DCR gain, which is exactly the shape of paying more for index work with no return. SECOND, base reads: Ddelta notes explicitly that reading base chunks for delta encoding causes random I/O, and their evaluation had to put dissimilar and delta chunks on SSD to measure maximum performance - i.e. the published throughput numbers are an SSD upper bound and degrade on slower media. Combined with the 30-90 MB/s encoding wall, the honest statement is that the delta pipeline's cost is dominated by index probes and random base reads, both of which grow with store size while the per-item computation stays flat. For this project's INGEST DEGRADATION question, this literature's answer is unambiguous: the standard remedy in the deduplication field for exactly this symptom is not to make the hashing faster but to attack the index probe - Bloom filters in front of the index, locality-preserving caching, sampled indexing, and stream-informed layout - and the correct diagnostic is hardware counters (cache misses, dTLB misses, page faults), not another call profile.
delta_cost_model: This item IS a delta cost model, so the exceptions matter more than usual. PER-CHANGE COST: given a base chunk and a target chunk already paired, Ddelta's encoding is O(len(chunk)) - a Gear pass at 32-byte average string granularity, a Spooky hash per string, a hash-table probe per string, plus greedy byte-wise extension at both ends of each match. Emitted output is proportional to the actual difference, so the OUTPUT is genuinely O(delta) even though the WORK is O(chunk). That distinction is the important one and it is usually elided: delta compression gives O(delta) storage, not O(delta) computation. CHANGES OUTSIDE THE MODEL, named: (1) PAIRING COST - finding the base is not in the model at all and is the expensive part; it is an index probe whose cost grows with store size, plus a random read of the base. A cost model that starts after pairing is describing the cheap half. (2) A change that resemblance detection MISSES - cost is not high, it is a silent loss of the delta entirely, and the miss rate is unmeasured (Finesse's analytic 33.3% for a first-sub-chunk edit, and near-total for a resized chunk, are the only figures available). (3) SIZE-CHANGING edits, which are precisely the ones the sub-chunk feature schemes handle worst, and precisely what a growing or shrinking DOM node does. (4) BASE-CHAIN reconstruction on read - unbounded unless capped, and outside every published cost model. (5) Changes to content the serialiser never emitted - CSS-driven, canvas, video, closed shadow roots, declarative shadow DOM flattened in the initial parse - produce identical bytes, an empty delta, and are NEVER DETECTED. Delta compression is blind to them in exactly the same way CDC is. (6) Attribute-only and interactive-state changes if state is not in the encoded stream. (7) For CARD only: model inference per chunk, plus the entire offline training cost, plus the unbounded cost of a retrain when the corpus drifts - none of which appear in any per-change accounting.
reanchoring_stability: This is the item's most useful contribution and also its most cautionary. Resemblance detection is precisely a re-anchoring mechanism: it identifies 'this content is a modified version of that content' without any address at all, which is the capability a single-xpath key entirely lacks. The measured behaviour under DOM-like change is discouraging for the naive versions and is stated analytically rather than empirically. Under Finesse, an edit touching the first sub-chunk's maximum value causes a feature mismatch with probability 33.3% by pure rank permutation; under N-transform, an edit that removes one of the top-k Rabin values replaces that feature outright; and crucially, two similar chunks OF DIFFERENT SIZES get different sub-chunk divisions and therefore mostly different features, so content that grew or shrank is systematically not re-anchored. CARD's fix - use the surrounding chunks' features as context so that a locally-damaged chunk is still recognised via its neighbourhood - is the right idea and maps naturally onto a trie (a node's siblings and parent as context), but CARD implements it as a trained BP-neural network with a hierarchical-softmax objective, which converts a deterministic exact-match test into a learned similarity score. That is exactly the unbounded fuzzy matching this project must avoid: it would contaminate the reproducibility claim, it has no confidence semantics that survive a retrain, and CARD itself reports the benefit vanishing on diffusely-changing data. The BOUNDED version that can be taken from this literature: use exact structural context as a tie-break, not a learned one - e.g. require an exact parent-address match or an exact sibling-content-hash match to confirm a content-based re-anchor - which keeps both legs exact-equality and yields a recordable confidence tier rather than a score. No measured DOM re-anchor rate exists anywhere in this family. [uncertain] on all re-anchor rates for web content.
adversarial_exposure: Fully layout-blind, so invisible-to-human content is preserved and delta-encoded exactly like visible content, with no ability to filter concealment without reading layout - the same structural exposure as CDC, and the same conclusion that a layout-blind fold is more exposed than the heuristic extractors it is compared against. Two additions specific to this item. NEGATIVE: resemblance detection is attacker-influenceable in a sharper way than chunking, because an adversary who controls page content can craft content whose super-features collide with a target's, forcing a pairing and thereby learning something about what else is in the store from whether the delta came out small. In a shared store this is a membership oracle. POSITIVE and genuinely useful: the same machinery is a strong cross-page injection detector - if a new node's content is resemblance-detected against a known-malicious payload, that is a signal no per-page analysis provides, and unlike an embedding it is a deterministic hash match. The asymmetry to respect is that this is safe to use as a DETECTOR (a positive finding is checkable by comparison) and unsafe to use as a FILTER (a negative finding is unmeasured).
provenance_carrying: None intrinsically, and delta encoding actively ENDANGERS provenance in a way plain chunking does not. A delta-encoded node's bytes exist only as instructions relative to another node, so per-token origin is not merely absent from the representation - it is split between two records, and reconstructing 'where did this token come from' requires walking the base chain. If the base belongs to a different url, a different capture time or a different gate state, then the delta-encoded node's content is physically interleaved with content of different provenance. For a project whose trie key already supplies url, xpath, capture time and shadow depth, the requirement is explicit and non-negotiable: the delta relation must be a recorded EDGE with its own provenance (base address, base capture time, encoder version, verification status), never an implicit storage detail, and no reconstruction may cross a gate-state or governance boundary silently. Get that right and provenance survives; leave the base pointer as an opaque storage id and it does not.
roundtrip_safety: Strong and checkable on the delta half: apply(base, encode(base, target)) == target is a hard fixed point, verifiable on every write, and it doubles as an oracle-free fidelity metric exactly as the field requires. Ddelta's design shows the pattern to copy - it uses a fast, weak hash for candidate matching and then verifies string CONTENT before emitting a copy instruction, so weak hashing never becomes a correctness risk. There is no escaping policy because there is no textual encoding; a delta is an instruction stream over byte offsets, so it has no injection surface of its own. The caveats are the same as CDC's plus one: an individual delta is meaningless without its base, so unlike a chunk it cannot be inspected, displayed or embedded in isolation at all, and a partially available base chain yields nothing rather than degraded content. Round-trip safety on the RESEMBLANCE half is not defined - there is no inverse operation to check.
token_budget_and_ordering: Nothing to offer directly - this layer is a storage representation, not a presentation one, and its output is never shown to a model. There are two indirect consequences worth stating. First, delta-encoded content must be fully materialised before it can be budgeted or truncated, so a store that delta-encodes aggressively pays reconstruction cost on every read path that a token budget touches - which argues for keeping the hot, model-visible tier undelta-ed and delta-encoding only cold history. Second, the resemblance index is a genuine ordering signal that is currently unused: knowing that node X is 95% identical to something the model has already seen this session is exactly the information needed to decide what NOT to re-emit under a budget, and it is available as an exact hash match rather than an embedding lookup. That is a real, cheap, deterministic deduplication-of-context mechanism, and it is the one thing in this item with direct bearing on the token contract.
representation_cost: Zero tokens - nothing here is ever emitted to a model. The costs are storage-side and they run in the opposite direction from CDC's: delta compression SAVES space (measured compression factors of 1.55x to 5.29x on top of deduplication across six datasets) at the price of index rows for the resemblance features, random base reads, and reconstruction latency. The exchange rate that matters for this project is that the saving is realised on cold, versioned, highly-similar content and the cost is paid on every read of hot content - so the correct scope is history and revisits, never the live fold.
what_could_be_adopted: Four things, in descending order of value, and one clear rejection. (1) THE 32-BYTE STRING GRANULARITY, as an empirical answer to the 'do CDC and a patricia trie compose, and at what cost' question. Ddelta's operating point is content-defined segmentation at an average of 32 BYTES per string, not 8 KB - deliberately chosen because compression ratio rises as string size falls, with encoding speed as the price. This is direct published evidence that content-defined boundaries work at DOM-node scale, which the storage-oriented CDC literature obscures by always defaulting to kilobyte targets. Take the granularity finding; it retargets the whole CDC adoption decision. (2) THE VERIFY-ON-WRITE PATTERN: use a fast weak hash to find candidate matches and then compare actual content before committing, so weak hashing costs time and never correctness. This is a no-mocks-compatible discipline that makes an entire class of probabilistic optimisation safe to adopt. (3) THE GREEDY-EXTENSION-FROM-BOTH-ENDS step, which found about one third of all redundancy with NO chunking and NO fingerprinting - a pure two-pointer scan inward from the ends of two byte strings. For comparing two versions of a node it is the cheapest possible first move, requires no index at all, and needs no parameters. (4) RESEMBLANCE MATCHING AS AN EXPLICIT, RECORDED SECOND RE-ANCHOR LEG, restricted to exact feature-hash equality and confirmed by an exact structural predicate (parent address or sibling content hash), yielding a discrete confidence tier rather than a score. REJECTED: CARD's BP-neural-network context model. The idea it embodies - that a node's neighbourhood helps re-identify it - is correct and worth taking in a deterministic form, but the implementation replaces an exact test with a learned one, is unreproducible without published weights, changes silently on retrain, and by the authors' own results contributes nothing where modifications are diffuse. Also worth carrying out of this item as a finding independent of any adoption: the deduplication field's diagnosis of index-probe cost as the invisible-to-profiler scaling wall, and its standard remedies, are the best available match for this project's measured ingest degradation.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS for Ddelta and classical resemblance detection: both are byte-level with no page-structure heuristic. CARD is a borderline violation in spirit rather than letter - its model learns structure from a training corpus, which is a pre-computed heuristic even though it is not hand-written about pages. Severity: none for Ddelta, medium for CARD. no_layout_in_the_fold -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS across the whole item. No geometry is read at any stage, and no stage could read it. Severity: none. o_delta -- ADOPTABLE IN THE ACTUATOR/STORAGE LAYER ONLY, with the pairing cost declared. Delta encoding gives O(delta) OUTPUT but O(chunk) WORK, and the pairing step that precedes it is an index probe plus a random base read whose cost grows with store size - so this family does not by itself deliver an O(delta) ingest guarantee and would, if adopted naively at ingest, add to the very index-growth cost that is currently degrading ingest. Verdict: use for cold history and revisit comparison, not on the hot ingest path. Severity: high if placed on the ingest path, low if scoped to history. no_mocks -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS for Ddelta and super-feature/Finesse detection: pure deterministic computation, no subsystem to stub, and the apply-and-compare check is a real oracle. REJECTED for CARD: a trained model with unpublished weights is a stub-shaped dependency in a measured path - it cannot be verified against ground truth, its output changes on retrain, and its failure mode is silent drift, which is precisely the class this project refuses. Severity: none for Ddelta, high for CARD. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS. Patches nothing, instruments nothing, is entirely post-capture and out of process; adds zero detection surface. Severity: none. OVERALL VERDICT: Ddelta's mechanisms are ADOPTABLE AS-IS in the storage/history layer (and its 32-byte granularity finding is adoptable as-is as an input to the CDC decision); classical resemblance detection is ADOPTABLE IN THE ACTUATOR/STORAGE LAYER ONLY with its miss rate instrumented rather than assumed; CARD is NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY - valuable for its demonstration that content-only features miss 33.3% of first-sub-chunk edits and nearly all size-changing edits, which is the argument for a second re-anchor leg, and rejected as an implementation.
governance_signal_handling: None, and not applicable - everything here is post-fetch. Two second-order interactions must be handled above this layer. First, delta encoding across urls entangles content whose source urls may carry different robots.txt, Content Signals, ai.txt or AIPREF terms, and unlike chunk sharing this entanglement is not symmetric - deleting the base breaks the delta. A governance-driven deletion must therefore materialise every dependent delta before removing its base, which is a real operational cost that must be budgeted, not discovered at deletion time. Second, the resemblance index is derived data that approximates content, so exporting it is closer to exporting the content than to exporting hashes, and any governance regime that restricts redistribution of page content should be read as restricting redistribution of the resemblance index too.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: The regulated act under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 is persistent storage of page content; delta encoding changes the storage form, not the fact, so any personal data present remains present and fully reconstructible. Three item-specific wrinkles. (1) DELETION IS HARDER THAN WITH DEDUPLICATION ALONE: erasing a record that serves as a delta base does not just leave a refcount problem, it breaks readers, so compliant deletion requires materialising dependents first - meaning an erasure request has a cost proportional to the base's fan-in, which should be bounded by capping chain depth and fan-in at write time. (2) THE RESEMBLANCE INDEX IS NOT ANONYMISED: super-features are locality-sensitive sketches of content, closer in character to an embedding than to a digest, and the encrypted-deduplication and chunking-attack literature already shows content partially recoverable from far weaker signals; a feature index over pages containing personal data should be treated as personal data. (3) CROSS-SUBJECT ENTANGLEMENT: delta-encoding one data subject's page against another's is a real possibility once resemblance is content-based rather than address-based, and it makes per-subject deletion and per-subject export both harder to reason about. [uncertain] on how EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 treat derived similarity indices specifically; the pseudonymisation direction of the guidance suggests they are in scope, but this was not verified against the text.
